title: Защитник с гипсом  (A Defender in a Cast)

segments.t: Stepping out into the courtyard behind the restaurant, Katya is harassed by two rude strangers passing by. Even though one of his arms is in a plaster cast, Denis rushes in to protect her, takes a punch, and scares the thugs away by shouting for the kitchen crew. Let's listen to their reconciliation in Russian.
Слушайте, отстаньте, мне сейчас не до вас.
Эй, вы что тут сейчас творите?
Быстро руки убрал от моей девушки!
А ну быстро ушли все отсюда!
Я сейчас сюда наших ребят позову!
Денис, скажи, тебе сейчас очень больно?
Подожди, дай я внимательно посмотрю.
Со мной всё нормально, совсем не больно.
Катя, прошу тебя, прости меня, пожалуйста.
Я правда никогда тебе не изменял.
Катя, я не хочу тебя потерять.
Тихо, я тебя уже давно простила.
Now let's trace how Denis defends Katya and wins her forgiveness line by line.
Слушайте, отстаньте, мне сейчас не до вас.
'Listen, back off, I have no time for you right now.' Outside, Katya tells two obnoxious men to leave her alone using a dative idiom.
Эй, вы что тут сейчас творите?
'Hey, what are you two doing right here?' Hearing the commotion, Denis runs over and confronts the two strangers.
Быстро руки убрал от моей девушки!
'Take your hands off my girlfriend right now!' A masculine past verb is used with imperative force to command immediate action.
А ну быстро ушли все отсюда!
'Come on, get out of here right now!' After taking a punch, Denis grabs a heavy pipe with his good hand and stands his ground.
Я сейчас сюда наших ребят позову!
'I will call our guys out here right now!' The animate accusative plural of guys serves as the direct object of the future verb will call.
Денис, скажи, тебе сейчас очень больно?
'Denis, tell me, does it hurt very much right now?' Once the thugs flee, Katya rushes to Denis's side using a dative predicate adverb.
Подожди, дай я внимательно посмотрю.
'Wait, let me take a careful look.' She gently touches his split lip using the imperative particle and a first-person future verb.
Со мной всё нормально, совсем не больно.
'Everything is fine with me, it does not hurt at all.' Denis winces slightly but insists that he feels no pain.
Катя, прошу тебя, прости меня, пожалуйста.
'Katya, I beg you, forgive me, please.' He uses a singular perfective imperative of forgiving with an accusative pronoun.
Я правда никогда тебе не изменял.
'I really never cheated on you.' He reassures her from the heart that he has always been faithful to her.
Катя, я не хочу тебя потерять.
'Katya, I do not want to lose you.' A negated verb of wanting governs a perfective infinitive and accusative pronoun.
Тихо, я тебя уже давно простила.
'Quiet, I forgave you a long time ago.' Katya smiles through her tears and hugs him with a feminine past perfective verb. Let's hear the courtyard scene between Denis and Katya from start to finish.

Touched by Denis's courage and devotion, Katya gently checks his bruised face and forgives him completely. Listen for the adverb meaning painful and the imperative meaning forgive. See you in the next scene.
